records.deidentified_narrative: a state trooper and gregg county sheriff's deputy were investigating a single vehicle crash that occurred on farm market [roadway] in gregg county (reference [case id]). the trooper, deputy, and the operator were standing on the north side of the roadway near the crashed vehicle. a total of three emergency vehicles were parked on both sides, with emergency lighting equipment activated for traffic control. unit 1 was traveling east on farm market 1252 approaching the crash scene. the trooper and deputy give visual ""stop"" signals to operators in both lanes so that they could escort the operator to the south side of the roadway. an operator traveling west observed them and stopped her vehicle, proving that the officers were visible and their signals clear. the operator of unit 1 did not slow however, and continued toward the trio as they walked south across the roadway. the trooper stopped near the center stripe divider and continued giving signals to try and stop, or at least slow, unit 1 down. operator of unit 1 began veering to [roadway] and struck the deputy as he was on the improved shoulder with unit 1's front right. operator of unit 1 exhibited signs of intoxication, and a subsequent field sobriety test indicated he was at a loss of mental and physical faculties due to drug consumption. operator of unit 1 was arrested for driving while intoxicated and booked into gregg county jail. operator of unit 1 provided a voluntary blood specimen; alcohol was not detected, drug analysis is pending. in this investigator's opinion, the deputy was on the improved shoulder when he was struck and thus, not illegally standing on the roadway. moreover, operator of unit 1 had more than sufficient time and distance to obey the stop signals given by both the deputy and the trooper. therefore, operator of unit 1 failed to control his speed as necessary to avoid colliding [roadway] and did not exercise due care.

47853147). k. adan was upset and said that a woman had accused her of hitting her with her vehicle (grey mercedez-benz tx license plate [identifier]). the alleged victim was not on scene. k. adan said that she did not hit anybody and that the woman was yelling at her. k. adan provided her information and then went to class in mcl. i provided k. adan with a business card with my name, badge number, email address, and [case id]. the alleged victim (the caller) identified as a twu affiliated employee was identified as rosa quiiano [date] then responded to the location with her supervisor. r. quiiano spoke broken english and her supervisor helped translate for her. r. quiiano said that she was walking in the mcl parking lot in the northwest section of the north parking lot when she was hit by k. adans vehicle. r. quiiano said that her left leg above her ankle is sore and that her foot got ran over. r. quiiano refused any [medical facility]. r. quiiano had bruising on her left leg above the ankle. cpl. marquez responded and spoke to r. quiiano and took a voluntary written statement from her about the collision. r. quiiano was in pain but refused to press charges for the collision. cpl. marquez took photographs of r. quiianos leg on scene. i took photographs of the vehicle on scene as well. i did not observe any damage to the vehicle or scuff marks either. r. quiiano was provided with a business card with my name, badge number, email address, and [case id]. i provided r. quiiano with k. adans vehicle insurance information as well (geico insurance policy # 41787035), dispatch confirmed that the insurance was valid. dispatch and cpl. marquez reviewed the cctv video from the mcl building and camera parking 99 on the northwest corner captured the collision at 12:41:25 hours. the video shows the vehicle rub against r. quiianos leg but it did not run over her foot or feet. r. quiiano also did not fall to the ground and there were no witnesses on scene that came over to assist. ofc. d. r. ames #1037september 9, 2024case # 24002914

records.deidentified_narrative: pedestrian (unit #2) was walking s/b in the parking lot at [roadway]. unit #1 was traveling e/b in the parking lot at [roadway]. driver#1 stated as she was traveling through the parking lot a vehicle began honking. driver#1 stated she turned to look at the person in the vehicle honking their horn. unit # 1 stated pedestrian ran in front of her vehicle. unit #1 stated she could not stop in time and struck the pedestrian. unit #1 stated pedestrian was on the opposite side of a parked vehicle when she attempted to cross through the parking lot. pedestrian's mother spoke with the investigating officer. the mother stated she began honking her horn as unit #2 drove by. the mother stated she was trying to get the driver of unit #1's attention because the pedestrian was crossing southbound through the parking lot. the mother stated the driver of unit #1's view of the pedestrian would have been obstructed due to a nearby parked car. the mother stated the pedestrian was traveling southbound through the parking lot from the opposite side of the park car when she was struck. aoi was determined by driver statements and pedestrian #1's mothers statement. officers investigation revealed pedestrian #1 failed to yield right of way and unit #2 contributed due to driver inattention.
